why: Standardised St John's wort extracts beat placebo in mild to moderate depression after several weeks, about as much as standard antidepressants.
source: Linde et al. 2008 Cochrane Database Syst Rev CD000448; Ng et al. 2017 J Affect Disord 210:211

why: As with other antidepressants, the mood benefit builds over weeks; a single dose does little.
source: Linde et al. 2008 Cochrane Database Syst Rev CD000448

why: One dose of St John's wort has no noticeable mood effect in healthy people.
source: Schmidt et al. 2000 Pharmacopsychiatry 33:47 (single-dose EEG/psychometric study)

why: Hyperforin raises extracellular serotonin in animal microdialysis; human brain data are lacking.
source: Kaehler et al. 1999 Neurosci Lett 262:199; Müller 2003 Pharmacol Res 47:101

why: Older trials found kava extract eased anxiety, but a large 2020 trial in generalised anxiety found no benefit over placebo.
source: Pittler & Ernst 2003 Cochrane Database Syst Rev CD003383; Sarris et al. 2020 J Clin Psychopharmacol 40:13

why: Benzodiazepines reliably dampen acute anxiety; kava's effect is small and inconsistent.
source: Baldwin et al. 2014 J Psychopharmacol 28:403; Sarris et al. 2020 J Clin Psychopharmacol 40:13

why: At usual doses kava causes little drowsiness compared with a benzodiazepine.
source: Sarris et al. 2012 Hum Psychopharmacol 27:262; Saletu et al. 1989 Hum Psychopharmacol 4:169

why: In controlled studies, usual doses of kava did not noticeably impair attention or memory.
source: Sarris et al. 2012 Hum Psychopharmacol 27:262; LaPorte et al. 2011 Phytomedicine 18:1080
